```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE,warning = FALSE,message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 9,fig.height = 6)
```

Yes. Given the structure of `acyls1`, I would build the R Markdown around **four layers**: whole-sample QC, lipid/class phenotypes, resolved fatty-acyl composition, and reproducibility-aware prioritisation. Importantly, the code below **flags** suspicious samples/results but does not automatically remove them. You then populate the manual exclusion vectors after inspecting the plots.

One assumption: I treat `X` as the lipid-species identifier and `nmolg` as the abundance. If `nmolg` is actually nmol/g rather than nmol, all fatty-acyl amounts retain that same denominator.

### 1. Setup and configuration

```{r 1. Setup and configuration}
# ============================================================
# LTP KO LIBRARY — LIPID / FATTY-ACYL ANALYSIS
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)

theme_set(
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95")
    )
)

options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)

OUTDIR <- "results_acyls1"
dir.create(OUTDIR, showWarnings = FALSE)
acyls1 = read_csv("~/Desktop/GitProjects/ltp_library_analysis/data/LTP_acyl_concentrations_raw1.csv")


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# USER SETTINGS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL_GENES <- paste0("NonTarget_", 1:6)

# Variables that represent experimental batch.
# The code will preferentially compare each KO with controls
# from the same Extraction / Roster.
BATCH_VARS <- c("Extraction", "Roster")
BATCH_VARS <- intersect(BATCH_VARS, names(acyls1))

# QC thresholds
MIN_REPLICATES <- 2

# Correlation of one replicate with the median of the other
# replicates from the same KO.
MIN_REPLICATE_CORRELATION <- 0.70

# Standard robust outlier threshold
ROBUST_Z_THRESHOLD <- 3.5

# With n = 3, 2/3 means at least two replicates agree
# on the direction of the effect.
MIN_SIGN_CONSISTENCY <- 2 / 3

# Number of features shown in large heatmaps
TOP_N_LIPIDS <- 50
TOP_N_FATTY_ACYLS <- 50
```

### 2. First inspect genes and controls

```{r}
gene_names <- acyls1 %>%
   distinct(Target.Gene.Symbol) %>%
   arrange(Target.Gene.Symbol)

print(gene_names)

if (!any(acyls1$Target.Gene.Symbol %in% CONTROL_GENES)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "None of CONTROL_GENES were found in Target.Gene.Symbol.\n",
      "Edit CONTROL_GENES at the top of the script."
    )
  )
}
```

### 3. Prepare the dataset

```{r}
# Expected number of lipid chains.
# Tails is used preferentially if it already contains this information.
# This lookup is only a fallback.

EXPECTED_TAILS <- c(
  "CE"   = 1,
  "FFA"  = 1,

  "LPC"  = 1,
  "LPE"  = 1,

  "PC"   = 2,
  "PE"   = 2,
  "PS"   = 2,
  "PI"   = 2,
  "PG"   = 2,
  "PA"   = 2,

  "DAG"  = 2,
  "TAG"  = 1,

  # Sphingolipids:
  # one N-linked fatty acid + sphingoid base
  "CER"  = 1,
  "DCER" = 1,
  "SM"   = 1,
  "HCER" = 1,
  "LCER" = 1
)

#BC add
acyls1 <- acyls1 %>% 
   mutate(X = paste0(Class, "(",Tails,")")) 

acyls_raw <- acyls1 %>%
  mutate(
    RowID = row_number(),
    Gene = as.character(Target.Gene.Symbol),
    Lipid = as.character(X),
    Class = as.character(Class),
    amount = as.numeric(nmolg),
    Group = if_else(
      Gene %in% CONTROL_GENES,
      "CTRL",
      Gene
    ),

    LipidKey = paste(Class, Lipid, sep = " | "),
    # Number of chains if Tails contains something such as 2 or "2 tails"
    ExpectedTailCount_from_Tails =
      readr::parse_number(as.character(Tails)),

    ExpectedTailCount_from_Class =
      as.numeric(EXPECTED_TAILS[Class]),

    ExpectedTailCount =
      coalesce(
        ExpectedTailCount_from_Tails,
        ExpectedTailCount_from_Class
      ),

    # Make a unique biological/sample identifier.
    SampleKey = paste(
      Gene,
      SampleID,
      Extraction,
      Roster,
      sep = "__"
    )
  ) %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(Gene),
    !is.na(Lipid),
    !is.na(Class),
    is.finite(amount),
    amount >= 0
  )


cat("Rows:", nrow(acyls_raw), "\n")
cat("Samples:", n_distinct(acyls_raw$SampleKey), "\n")
cat("Genes:", n_distinct(acyls_raw$Gene), "\n")
cat("Lipid species:", n_distinct(acyls_raw$LipidKey), "\n")
cat("Classes:", n_distinct(acyls_raw$Class), "\n")
```

### 4. Some helper functions
These make the later analysis much cleaner.
```{r}
# ============================================================
# HELPER FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================
half_min_positive <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x) & x > 0]
  if (length(x) == 0)
    return(1e-12)
  min(x) / 2
}


robust_z <- function(x) {
  med <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  s <- mad(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(s) || s == 0) {
    return(rep(0, length(x)))
  }
  (x - med) / s
}


safe_cor <- function(x, y,method = "spearman") {
  ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)
  if (sum(ok) < 5)
    return(NA_real_)
  if (sd(x[ok]) == 0 ||
      sd(y[ok]) == 0)
    return(NA_real_)
  cor( x[ok], y[ok], method = method)
}


sign_consistency <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) < 2)
    return(NA_real_)
  med <- median(x)
  if (med == 0)
    return(NA_real_)
  mean(sign(x) == sign(med))
}
```

This function calculates a control-normalised effect while preferentially using controls from the same `Extraction`/`Roster`.

```{r}
add_control_effect <- function(tbl,
                               feature_cols,
                               value_col = "value",
                               effect_type = c(
                                 "log2fc",
                                 "difference"
                               ),
                               batch_vars = BATCH_VARS) {

  effect_type <- match.arg(effect_type)
  feature_cols <- unique(feature_cols)
  batch_vars <- unique(batch_vars)
  dat <- tbl
  
  # ----------------------------------
  # Transformation
  # ----------------------------------
  
  if (effect_type == "log2fc") {
    pseudocounts <- dat %>%
      group_by(
        across(
          all_of(feature_cols)
        )
      ) %>%
      summarise(
        .pseudo =
          half_min_positive(
            .data[[value_col]]
          ),
        .groups = "drop"
      )

    dat <- dat %>%
      left_join(
        pseudocounts,
        by = feature_cols
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        .analysis_value =
          log2(
            .data[[value_col]] +
            .pseudo
          )
      )

  } else {

    dat <- dat %>%
      mutate(
        .analysis_value =
          .data[[value_col]]
      )
  }


  # ----------------------------------
  # Matched controls
  # ----------------------------------

  matched_keys <- unique(
    c(
      batch_vars,
      feature_cols
    )
  )


  ctrl_matched <- dat %>%
    filter(Group == "CTRL") %>%
    group_by(
      across(
        all_of(matched_keys)
      )
    ) %>%

    summarise(
      .ctrl_matched =
        median(
          .analysis_value,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )


  # ----------------------------------
  # Global controls
  # Used if no matched control exists
  # ----------------------------------

  ctrl_global <- dat %>%
    filter(Group == "CTRL") %>%
    group_by(
      across(
        all_of(feature_cols)
      )
    ) %>%
    summarise(
      .ctrl_global =
        median(
          .analysis_value,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

    dat %>%
    left_join(
      ctrl_matched,
      by = matched_keys
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      ctrl_global,
      by = feature_cols
    ) %>%

    mutate(
      ControlReference =
        coalesce(
          .ctrl_matched,
          .ctrl_global
        ),
      effect =
        .analysis_value -
        ControlReference,
      ControlSource = case_when(
        !is.na(.ctrl_matched) ~
          "matched batch",
        !is.na(.ctrl_global) ~
          "global fallback",
        TRUE ~
          "no control"
      )
    )
}
```

And one generic reproducibility summariser:

```{r}
summarise_gene_effect <- function(tbl,
                                  feature_cols) {
  tbl %>%
    filter(
      Group != "CTRL",
      is.finite(effect)
    ) %>%
    group_by(
      Gene,
      across(
        all_of(feature_cols)
      )
    ) %>%
    summarise(
      n_rep =
        n_distinct(SampleKey),
      effect_median =
        median(
          effect,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      effect_mean =
        mean(
          effect,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      effect_sd =
        sd(
          effect,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      effect_mad =
        mad(
          effect,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      effect_iqr =
        IQR(
          effect,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      sign_consistency =
        sign_consistency(effect),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      reproducible =
        n_rep >= MIN_REPLICATES &
        sign_consistency >=
        MIN_SIGN_CONSISTENCY
    )
}
```

# Part I — Sample-level QC

### 5. Build sample × lipid matrix

```{r}
species_raw <- acyls_raw %>%
  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Group,
    SampleID,
    across(
      all_of(BATCH_VARS)
    ),
    Class,
    Lipid,
    LipidKey
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    amount =
      sum(
        amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


lipid_pseudocounts <- species_raw %>%
  group_by(LipidKey) %>%
  summarise(
    pseudo =
      half_min_positive(amount),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

species_raw <- species_raw %>%
  left_join(
    lipid_pseudocounts,
    by = "LipidKey"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    log2_amount =
      log2(
        amount +
        pseudo
      )
  )
```

### 6. Sample totals

```{r}
sample_qc <- species_raw %>%
  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Group,
    SampleID,
    across(
      all_of(BATCH_VARS)
    )
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    TotalAmount =
      sum(
        amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    DetectedLipids =
      sum(
        amount > 0,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    MedianLipidAmount =
      median(
        amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sample_qc <- sample_qc %>%
  mutate(
    log2Total =
      log2(
        TotalAmount +
        half_min_positive(
          TotalAmount
        )
      ),

    TotalAmount_Z =
      robust_z(log2Total),
    DetectedLipids_Z =
      robust_z(DetectedLipids)
  )
```

### 7. Replicate-to-consensus correlations

For each biological replicate, this compares its complete lipidomic profile with the median profile of the **other replicates of the same gene**.

This is particularly useful for your library.

```{r}
lipid_wide <- species_raw %>%
  select(
    SampleKey,
    LipidKey,
    log2_amount
  ) %>%

  pivot_wider(
    names_from = LipidKey,
    values_from = log2_amount,
    values_fill = NA_real_
  )

sample_ids <-
  lipid_wide$SampleKey

lipid_matrix <-
  lipid_wide %>%
  select(-SampleKey) %>%
  as.matrix()

rownames(lipid_matrix) <-
  sample_ids

sample_metadata <- species_raw %>%
  distinct(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Group,
    SampleID,
    across(
      all_of(BATCH_VARS)
    )
  )

consensus_correlations <-
  map_dfr(
    unique(sample_metadata$Gene),

    function(gene_i) {
      ids <-
        sample_metadata %>%
        filter(Gene == gene_i) %>%
        pull(SampleKey)

      if (length(ids) < 2) {
        return(
          tibble(
            SampleKey = ids,
            ReplicateConsensusR =
              NA_real_
          )
        )
      }

      map_dfr(
        ids,
        function(id_i) {
          other_ids <-
            setdiff(
              ids,
              id_i
            )
          consensus <-
            apply(lipid_matrix[other_ids,,drop = FALSE],2,median,na.rm = TRUE)
          r <-
            safe_cor(lipid_matrix[id_i,],consensus,method = "spearman")


          tibble(
            SampleKey = id_i,
            ReplicateConsensusR = r
          )
        }
      )
    }
  )
```

### 8. PCA

PCA is only being used for QC/visualisation. Missing measurements are median-imputed **only for the PCA**.

```{r}
pca_matrix <-lipid_matrix
for (j in seq_len(ncol(pca_matrix))) {
  replacement <-
    median(
      pca_matrix[, j],
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  if (!is.finite(replacement))
    replacement <- 0

  pca_matrix[
    is.na(pca_matrix[, j]),
    j
  ] <- replacement
}

# Remove zero-variance features
keep <-
  apply(pca_matrix,2,sd) > 0

pca_matrix <-
  pca_matrix[, keep, drop = FALSE]

pca_fit <-
  prcomp(
    pca_matrix,
    center = TRUE,
    scale. = TRUE
  )

pca_scores <-
  as_tibble(pca_fit$x,rownames = "SampleKey") %>%
  left_join(sample_metadata,by = "SampleKey")


variance_explained <-
  100 *pca_fit$sdev^2 /sum(pca_fit$sdev^2)
```

### 9. Combine QC metrics and flag suspicious samples

```{r}
qc_table <- sample_qc %>%
  left_join(
    consensus_correlations,
    by = "SampleKey"
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    FlagTotalAmount =
      abs(TotalAmount_Z) >
      ROBUST_Z_THRESHOLD,

    FlagDetectedLipids =
      abs(DetectedLipids_Z) >
      ROBUST_Z_THRESHOLD,

    FlagReplicateCorrelation =
      !is.na(ReplicateConsensusR) &
      ReplicateConsensusR <
      MIN_REPLICATE_CORRELATION,

    QC_Flag =
      FlagTotalAmount |
      FlagDetectedLipids |
      FlagReplicateCorrelation
  )


qc_candidates <- qc_table %>%
  filter(QC_Flag) %>%
  arrange(
    ReplicateConsensusR
  )


print(
  qc_candidates,
  n = Inf
)


write_csv(
  qc_candidates,
  file.path(
    OUTDIR,
    "QC_candidate_outliers.csv"
  )
)
```

### 10. QC plots

```{r}
ggplot(qc_table,
  aes(x = DetectedLipids,y = TotalAmount)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(shape = QC_Flag),size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data =qc_table %>% filter(QC_Flag),

    aes(label =paste(Gene,SampleID,sep = " / ")),

    size = 3,max.overlaps = Inf) +
   scale_y_log10() +
   labs(
    title =
      "Lipidomics sample QC",
    x =
      "Number of detected lipid species",
    y =
      "Total measured lipid abundance",
    shape =
      "QC flag"
  )
```

Replicate reproducibility:

```{r}
gene_repro_order <- qc_table %>%
  group_by(Gene) %>%
  summarise(
    median_r =
      median(
        ReplicateConsensusR,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  arrange(median_r) %>%

  pull(Gene)


qc_table <- qc_table %>%
  mutate(
    Gene_QC =
      factor(
        Gene,
        levels =
          gene_repro_order
      )
  )


ggplot(
  qc_table,
  aes(
    x = Gene_QC,
    y = ReplicateConsensusR
  )
) +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept =
      MIN_REPLICATE_CORRELATION,
    linetype = 2
  ) +

  geom_point(
    position =
      position_jitter(
        width = 0.15
      ),
    size = 2
  ) +

  geom_text_repel(
    data =
      qc_table %>%
      filter(
        FlagReplicateCorrelation
      ),

    aes(
      label =
        paste(
          Gene,
          SampleID,
          sep = " / "
        )
    ),

    size = 2.5,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +

  coord_flip() +

  labs(
    title =
      "Reproducibility of biological replicates",
    subtitle =
      "Each sample is correlated with the median lipidome of the other replicates of the same KO",
    x = NULL,
    y =
      "Spearman correlation with replicate consensus"
  )
```

PCA:

```{r}
pca_plot_data <- pca_scores %>%

  left_join(
    qc_table %>%
      select(
        SampleKey,
        QC_Flag
      ),
    by = "SampleKey"
  )


ggplot(
  pca_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = PC1,
    y = PC2
  )
) +

  geom_point(
    aes(
      shape = QC_Flag
    ),

  ) +

        )

  ) +

  labs(
    title =

  )
```

# Part II — Manual exclusions

This is the part I would edit **after looking at the QC plots**.

I strongly recommend excluding an individual sample rather than the whole gene whenever possible.

```{r}
# ============================================================
# MANUAL EXCLUSIONS
# ============================================================
# 
# # Remove a complete KO only if there is a clear technical reason.
# EXCLUDE_GENES <- c(
#   # "GENE1",
#   # "GENE2"
# )
# 
# 
# # Best option:
# # copy SampleKey directly from qc_candidates.
# EXCLUDE_SAMPLES <- c(
#   # "GENE1__A1__Extraction1__Roster1"
# )
# 
# 
# # Alternatively identify individual samples by Gene + SampleID.

#   # Example:
```

# Part III — Lipid-class abundance

### 11. Total amount per lipid class

```{r}
class_sample <- acyls_clean %>%

  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Group,
    SampleID,
    across(
      all_of(BATCH_VARS)
    ),
    Class
  ) %>%

  summarise(
    value =
      sum(
        amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Calculate log2 fold change against matched controls:

```{r}
class_effect <- add_control_effect(
  class_sample,
  feature_cols =
    "Class",
  value_col =
    "value",
  effect_type =
    "log2fc"
)


class_gene <- summarise_gene_effect(
  class_effect,
  feature_cols =
    "Class"
)
```

Inspect:

```{r}
class_gene %>%
  arrange(
    desc(
      abs(
        effect_median
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  print(n = 50)
```

### 12. Class-level heatmap

Low-reproducibility effects are faded rather than deleted.

```{r}
gene_order <- class_gene %>%
  group_by(Gene) %>%
  summarise(phenotype =sqrt(mean(effect_median^2,na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(phenotype) %>%
  pull(Gene)


class_gene_plot <- class_gene %>%
   mutate(Gene =factor(Gene,levels =gene_order),
          plot_alpha = if_else(reproducible,1,0))


ggplot(
  class_gene_plot,
  aes(
    x = Class,
    y = Gene,
    fill = effect_median,
    alpha = plot_alpha
  )
) +

  geom_tile() +

  scale_fill_gradient2(
    midpoint = 0,
    name =
      "Median\nlog2 FC"
  ) +

  scale_alpha_identity() +

  labs(
    title =
      "Lipid-class phenotypes across the LTP KO library",
    subtitle =
      "Green cells indicate poor replicate consistency",
   x = NULL,
    y = NULL) +
   theme_classic()+
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = 'green')) 
```

# Part IV — Individual lipid-species phenotypes

### 13. Lipid-species log2FC

```{r}
species_clean <- acyls_clean %>%
  group_by(
    SampleKey, Gene, Group, SampleID,
    across(all_of(BATCH_VARS)),
    Class,Lipid,LipidKey) %>%
  summarise(value =sum(amount,na.rm = TRUE),.groups = "drop")


species_effect <- add_control_effect(species_clean,
  feature_cols = c(
      "Class","Lipid","LipidKey"
    ),
  value_col ="value",
  effect_type ="log2fc"
)


species_gene <- summarise_gene_effect(
  species_effect,
  feature_cols =
    c(
      "Class",
      "Lipid",
      "LipidKey"
    )
)
```

Select the most informative lipid species:

```{r}
top_lipids <- species_gene %>% 
  group_by(LipidKey) %>%
  summarise(
    phenotype_score =
      median(
        abs(
          effect_median
        ),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  slice_max(phenotype_score, n = TOP_N_LIPIDS) %>%
  pull(LipidKey)
```

```{r}
ggplot(
   species_gene %>% filter(LipidKey %in% top_lipids),
   aes(x = LipidKey,y = Gene,fill = effect_median,#color = effect_median,
       alpha =if_else(reproducible,1,0.2))) +
   geom_point(shape = 21) +
   scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = 0, name ="log2 FC") +
   #scale_color_gradient2(midpoint = 0, name ="log2 FC") +
   scale_alpha_identity() +
   labs(title ="Strongest lipid-species phenotypes",
        x = NULL,y = NULL) +
   theme(axis.text.x =element_text(angle = 90,hjust = 1,vjust = 0.5,size = 6),
         axis.text.y =element_text(size = 6))
```

---

# Part V — Convert lipids into resolved fatty-acyl molecules

This is the important part for saturation/PUFA analysis.

For example:

```text
10 units PC(14:0/20:2)
```

becomes:
```text
10 units 14:0
10 units 20:2
```

while:

```text
10 units PC(16:0/16:0)
```

becomes:

```text
20 units 16:0
```

### 14. Convert Tail_1 and Tail_2 to long format

```{r}
common_cols <- unique(
  c(
    "RowID",
    "SampleKey",
    "Gene",
    "Group",
    "SampleID",
    BATCH_VARS,
    "Class",
    "Lipid",
    "amount",
    "ExpectedTailCount"
  )
)


tail1 <- acyls_clean %>% 
  transmute(
     across(
      all_of(common_cols)
    ),
    TailPosition = 1L,
    FattyAcyl =
      as.character(
        Tail_1
      ),

    FA_length =
      as.numeric(
        Tail_1_length
      ),

    FA_bend =
      as.numeric(
        Tail_1_bend
      )
  )


tail2 <- acyls_clean %>% 
  transmute(
    across(
      all_of(common_cols)
    ),
    TailPosition = 2L,
    FattyAcyl =
      as.character(
        Tail_2
      ),
    FA_length =
      as.numeric(
        Tail_2_length
      ),
    FA_bend =
      as.numeric(
        Tail_2_bend
      )
  )


acyl_long_all <- bind_rows(
  tail1,
  tail2
)
```

### 15. Recognise fatty acids, ether chains and sphingoid bases

This prevents `d18:1` in SM/Cer from being counted as an 18:1 fatty acid.

```{r}

nrow(acyl_long_all)
acyl_long_all = acyl_long_all %>%  
   filter(!is.na(FattyAcyl))
nrow(acyl_long_all)

acyl_long_all <- acyl_long_all %>%
   mutate( 
      # FattyAcyl = na_if(FattyAcyl,""),
      ChainType = case_when(
         str_detect(Class,regex("^PEO",ignore_case = TRUE)) ~"Ether-linked chain",      
         str_detect(Class,regex("^PEP",ignore_case = TRUE)) ~"Ether-linked chain",
         str_detect(Class,regex("^SM",ignore_case = TRUE)) ~"Sphingoid-linked",
         str_detect(Class,regex("CER",ignore_case = TRUE)) ~"Sphingoid-linked",
         
         #str_detect(FattyAcyl,"^(FA)?[0-9]+:[0-9]+") ~"Fatty acyl",
         #is.na(FattyAcyl) ~ "Fatty acyl",
         TRUE ~ "Fatty acyl"
      )
      
      # Parse length from annotation if missing
      #FA_length = coalesce(FA_length, readr::parse_number(FattyAcyl)),
      
      # Parse number of double bonds if missing
      #FA_bend = coalesce(FA_bend,as.numeric(str_match(FattyAcyl,":(\\d+)")[, 2] )),
      #FA =FattyAcyl %>%str_remove("^FA")
   )
```

Check how the annotations were classified:

```{r}
acyl_long_all %>% 
   count(ChainType) %>%
   arrange(desc(n))
```

---

# Part VI — Annotation coverage

This is particularly relevant for species such as:
`TAG48:0-FA18:0`
where only one of three chains may be identified.
### 16. Calculate resolved-chain coverage

```{r}
annotation_coverage <- acyl_long_all %>%
  group_by(RowID) %>%
  summarise(
    ResolvedChains =
      sum(
        ChainType !=
          "Unresolved" &
        !is.na(FattyAcyl)
      ),

    ResolvedFattyAcyls =
      sum(
        ChainType ==
          "Fatty acyl"
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


coverage_table <- acyls_clean %>%

  select(
    RowID,
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    SampleID,
    Class,
    Lipid,
    amount,
    ExpectedTailCount
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    annotation_coverage,
    by = "RowID"
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    AnnotationCoverage =
      if_else(
        !is.na(
          ExpectedTailCount
        ) &
        ExpectedTailCount > 0,

        pmin(
          ResolvedChains /
            ExpectedTailCount,
          1
        ),

        NA_real_
      )
  )
```

Abundance-weighted annotation coverage:

```{r}
coverage_sample <- coverage_table %>%

  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    SampleID,
    Class
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    AnnotationCoverage =
      weighted.mean(
        AnnotationCoverage,
        w = amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  coverage_sample,
  aes(
    x = Class,
    y =
      100 *
      AnnotationCoverage
  )
) +

  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +

  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    alpha = 0.4,
    size = 1
  ) +

  labs(
    title =
      "Fatty-chain annotation coverage",
    y =
      "% of expected chains resolved",
    x = NULL
  )
```

This is an important figure because it tells you which classes are actually suitable for individual fatty-acyl analysis.

---

# Part VII — Fatty-acyl amounts
### 17. Keep true ester-linked fatty acids

```{r}
fa_long <- acyl_long_all %>%
  filter(
    ChainType ==
      "Fatty acyl",
    !is.na(FA_length),
    !is.na(FA_bend)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Standard biochemical definition:
    # PUFA = two or more double bonds
    Saturation = case_when(

      FA_bend == 0 ~
        "SFA",

      FA_bend == 1 ~
        "MUFA",

      FA_bend >= 2 ~
        "PUFA",

      TRUE ~
        NA_character_
    ),

    Saturation =
      factor(
        Saturation,
        levels =
          c(
            "SFA",
            "MUFA",
            "PUFA"
          )
      ),

    DB_group = case_when(
      FA_bend == 0 ~ "0",
      FA_bend == 1 ~ "1",
      FA_bend == 2 ~ "2",
      FA_bend == 3 ~ "3",
      FA_bend == 4 ~ "4",
      FA_bend == 5 ~ "5",
      FA_bend >= 6 ~ "6+"
    ),

    ChainLengthGroup = case_when(
      FA_length < 16 ~ "<16",
      FA_length == 16 ~ "16",
      FA_length == 18 ~ "18",
      FA_length == 20 ~ "20",
      FA_length == 22 ~ "22",
      FA_length >= 24 ~ "24+",
      TRUE ~ "other"
    )
  )
```

### 18. Calculate amount of each fatty acid

Because each tail carries the amount of the parent lipid, duplicate chains are automatically counted correctly.

```{r}
fa_amount_class <- fa_long %>%
  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Group,
    SampleID,
    across(
      all_of(BATCH_VARS)
    ),
    Class,
    FattyAcyl,
    FA_length,
    FA_bend,
    Saturation
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    FA_amount =
      sum(
        amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### 19. Fatty-acyl percentages within each class

```{r}
fa_amount_class <- fa_amount_class %>%
  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Class
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    TotalResolvedFA =
      sum(
        FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    FA_percent =
      100 *
      FA_amount /
      TotalResolvedFA
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

You now have, for every sample:

```text
PC / 16:0 / amount
PC / 16:0 / %
PC / 18:1 / amount
PC / 18:1 / %
PC / 20:4 / amount
...
```

# Part IX — SFA, MUFA and PUFA

### 20. Class-specific saturation profile

```{r}
saturation_class <- fa_amount_class %>%
  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Group,
    SampleID,
    across(
      all_of(BATCH_VARS)
    ),
    Class,
    Saturation
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    FA_amount =
      sum(
        FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Class
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    Percent =
      100 *
      FA_amount /
      sum(
        FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

### 21. Control-normalised SFA/MUFA/PUFA amounts

```{r}
saturation_amount_effect <- saturation_class %>%
  rename(
    value =

  add_control_effect(
    feature_cols =

      ),
    value_col =

    effect_type =

  )


saturation_amount_gene <-
  summarise_gene_effect(
    saturation_amount_effect,
    feature_cols =
      c(
        "Class",
        "Saturation"
      )
  )
```

### 22. Control-normalised saturation percentages

Percentages should be analysed as **percentage-point differences**, not fold changes.

```{r}

  saturation_class %>%
  rename(

  add_control_effect(
    feature_cols =
      c(

        "Saturation"
      ),
    value_col =
      "value",
    effect_type =
      "difference"
  )


saturation_percent_gene <-
  summarise_gene_effect(

    feature_cols =
      c(
        "Class",
        "Saturation"
      )
  )
```

# Part X — Unsaturation index and chain length

This is probably one of the most useful analyses for the library.

### 24. Calculate class-specific structural metrics

```{r}
fa_metrics <- fa_amount_class %>%

  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Group,
    SampleID,
    across(
      all_of(BATCH_VARS)
    ),
    Class
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    TotalResolvedFA =
      sum(
        FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    # Mean number of double bonds
    # per resolved fatty-acyl chain
    UnsaturationIndex =
      weighted.mean(
        FA_bend,
        w =
          FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    MeanChainLength =
      weighted.mean(
        FA_length,
        w =
          FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    SFA_percent =
      100 *
      sum(
        FA_amount[
          FA_bend == 0
        ],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) /
      sum(
        FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    MUFA_percent =
      100 *
      sum(
        FA_amount[
          FA_bend == 1
        ],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) /
      sum(
        FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    PUFA_percent =
      100 *
      sum(
        FA_amount[
          FA_bend >= 2
        ],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) /
      sum(
        FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    # Highly unsaturated fatty acids
    HUFA_percent =
      100 *
      sum(
        FA_amount[
          FA_bend >= 4
        ],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) /
      sum(
        FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    # Very-long-chain fatty acids
    VLCFA_percent =
      100 *
      sum(
        FA_amount[
          FA_length >= 22
        ],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) /
      sum(
        FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    C24plus_percent =
      100 *
      sum(
        FA_amount[
          FA_length >= 24
        ],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) /
      sum(
        FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Convert to long format:

```{r}
fa_metrics_long <- fa_metrics %>%

  pivot_longer(

    cols =
      c(
        UnsaturationIndex,
        MeanChainLength,
        SFA_percent,
        MUFA_percent,
        PUFA_percent,
        HUFA_percent,
        VLCFA_percent,
        C24plus_percent
      ),

    names_to =
      "Metric",

    values_to =
      "value"
  )
```

### 25. Calculate differences from controls

```{r}
fa_metric_effect <- add_control_effect(
  fa_metrics_long,
  feature_cols =
    c(
      "Class",
      "Metric"
    ),
  value_col =
    "value",
  effect_type =
    "difference"
)


fa_metric_gene <- summarise_gene_effect(
  fa_metric_effect,
  feature_cols =
    c(
      "Class",
      "Metric"
    )
)
```

# Part XIV — Exact double-bond distributions

This lets you distinguish changes in 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6+ double-bond fatty acids.

```{r}
db_distribution <- fa_amount_class %>%

  mutate(

    DB_group = case_when(
      FA_bend == 0 ~ "0",
      FA_bend == 1 ~ "1",
      FA_bend == 2 ~ "2",
      FA_bend == 3 ~ "3",
      FA_bend == 4 ~ "4",
      FA_bend == 5 ~ "5",
      FA_bend >= 6 ~ "6+"
    ),

    DB_group =
      factor(
        DB_group,
        levels =
          c(
            "0",
            "1",
            "2",
            "3",
            "4",
            "5",
            "6+"
          )
      )
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Group,
    SampleID,
    across(
      all_of(BATCH_VARS)
    ),
    Class,
    DB_group
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    amount =
      sum(
        FA_amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Class
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    Percent =
      100 *
      amount /
      sum(
        amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
  ) %>%

  ungroup()
```

Control-normalise:

```{r}
db_effect <- db_distribution %>%

  rename(
    value =
      Percent
  ) %>%

  add_control_effect(
    feature_cols =
      c(
        "Class",
        "DB_group"
      ),
    effect_type =
      "difference"
  )


db_gene <- summarise_gene_effect(
  db_effect,
  feature_cols =
    c(
      "Class",
      "DB_group"
    )
)
```

# Part XVI — Find the strongest fatty-acyl phenotypes

```{r}
top_fa_features <-
  fa_specific_gene %>%

  mutate(
    Feature =
      paste(
        Class,
        FattyAcyl,
        sep = " | "
      )
  ) %>%

  group_by(Feature) %>%

  summarise(

    score =
      median(
        abs(
          effect_median
        ),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  slice_max(
    score,
    n =
      TOP_N_FATTY_ACYLS
  ) %>%

  pull(Feature)
```

# Part XVIII — Inspect replicate behaviour of top hits

This is where I would explicitly look for cases where one replicate is producing an apparently interesting result.

For example, PUFA:

```{r}
top_pufa_hits <- fa_metric_gene %>%
  filter(
    Metric ==
      "PUFA_percent"
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    desc(
      abs(
        effect_median
      )
    )
  ) %>%

  slice_head(
    n = 25
  ) %>%

  transmute(
    Gene,
    Class,
    Hit =
      paste(
        Gene,
        Class,
        sep = " | "
      )
  )


pufa_samples <- fa_metric_effect %>%

  filter(
    Metric ==
      "PUFA_percent",
    Group != "CTRL"
  ) %>%

  inner_join(
    top_pufa_hits,
    by =
      c(
        "Gene",
        "Class"
      )
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  pufa_samples,
  aes(
    x = Hit,
    y = effect
  )
) +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = 2
  ) +

  geom_point(
    position =
      position_jitter(
        width = 0.12
      ),
    size = 2
  ) +

  geom_text_repel(
    aes(
      label =
        SampleID
    ),
    size = 2.5,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +

  coord_flip() +

  labs(
    title =
      "Replicate-level behaviour of strongest PUFA phenotypes",
    subtitle =
      "Sample labels make single-replicate outliers easy to identify",
    x = NULL,
    y =
      "Δ PUFA percentage points vs control"
  )
```

You can use the same approach for unsaturation:

```{r}
unsaturation_samples <- fa_metric_effect %>%

  filter(

    Group != "CTRL"

  inner_join(

ggplot(

      ),

  ) +

  geom_text_repel(

        SampleID
```

# Part XIX — Find explicitly non-reproducible results

This produces the table I would inspect before claiming a phenotype.

```{r}
poorly_reproduced_metrics <- fa_metric_gene %>%
  filter(
    n_rep >=
      MIN_REPLICATES,
    !reproducible
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    desc(
      abs(
        effect_median
      )
    )
  )


print(
  poorly_reproduced_metrics,
  n = 100
)


write_csv(
  poorly_reproduced_metrics,
  file.path(
    OUTDIR,
    "nonreproducible_FA_metrics.csv"
  )
)
```

More specifically, find results where replicates disagree on direction:

```{R}
discordant_results <- fa_metric_gene %>%

  filter(
    n_rep >= 3,
    sign_consistency < 1
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    sign_consistency,
    desc(
      abs(
        effect_median
      )
    )
  )


print(
  discordant_results,
  n = 100
)
```

That is particularly useful with three replicates because:

* `1.00` = all three agree on direction
* `0.67` = two agree, one disagrees

I would generally treat the latter as **something to inspect manually**, rather than automatically discard.

---

# Part XX — Molecular unsaturation using `Total_tail_bend`

I would analyse this separately from fatty-acyl PUFA.

`Total_tail_bend = 2` does **not** necessarily mean a PUFA-containing lipid. For example:

```text
PC(18:1/18:1)
```

has:

```text
Total_tail_bend = 2
```

but contains two MUFAs.

Nevertheless, the total molecular double-bond distribution is biologically useful.

```{R}
molecular_metrics <- acyls_clean %>%

  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Group,
    SampleID,
    across(
      all_of(BATCH_VARS)
    ),
    Class
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    MeanTotalTailLength =
      weighted.mean(
        Total_tail_length,
        w =
          amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    MeanTotalDoubleBonds =
      weighted.mean(
        Total_tail_bend,
        w =
          amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    Molecular_DB0_percent =
      100 *
      sum(
        amount[
          Total_tail_bend == 0
        ],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) /
      sum(
        amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    Molecular_DB1_percent =
      100 *
      sum(
        amount[
          Total_tail_bend == 1
        ],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) /
      sum(
        amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    Molecular_DB2plus_percent =
      100 *
      sum(
        amount[
          Total_tail_bend >= 2
        ],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) /
      sum(
        amount,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

# Part XXI — Rank LTPs by strength AND reproducibility

This is useful for discovering candidates beyond the obvious ORP9/ORP11-type phenotypes.

### 28. Overall lipid-class phenotype strength

```{R}
gene_class_score <- class_gene %>%
  group_by(Gene) %>%

  summarise(

    ClassPhenotypeStrength =
      sqrt(
        mean(
          effect_median^2,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      ),

    ReproducibleClassFraction =
      mean(
        reproducible,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Add whole-lipidome replicate correlation:

```{R}
gene_replicate_score <- qc_table %>%

  filter(
    Group != "CTRL"
  ) %>%

  group_by(Gene) %>%

  summarise(

    MedianReplicateCorrelation =
      median(
        ReplicateConsensusR,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Combine:

```{R}
gene_priority <- gene_class_score %>%

  left_join(
    gene_replicate_score,
    by = "Gene"
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    desc(
      ClassPhenotypeStrength
    )
  )


write_csv(
  gene_priority,
  file.path(
    OUTDIR,
    "LTP_phenotype_priority.csv"
  )
)
```

Plot:

```{R}
ggplot(
  gene_priority,
  aes(
    x =
      MedianReplicateCorrelation,
    y =
      ClassPhenotypeStrength
  )
) +

  geom_point(
    aes(
      size =
        ReproducibleClassFraction
    ),
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +

  geom_text_repel(

    data =
      gene_priority %>%
      slice_max(
        ClassPhenotypeStrength,
        n = 20
      ),

    aes(
      label = Gene
    ),

    max.overlaps = Inf,
    size = 3
  ) +

  labs(
    title =
      "Prioritising LTP lipidomic phenotypes",
    x =
      "Median replicate lipidome correlation",
    y =
      "Overall lipid-class phenotype strength",
    size =
      "Fraction reproducible"
  )
```

This plot should be particularly informative:

**upper right = strong + reproducible phenotype**.

# Part XXII — A saturation-specific LTP ranking

```{R}
saturation_priority <- fa_metric_gene %>%

  filter(
    Metric %in%
      c(
        "UnsaturationIndex",
        "PUFA_percent",
        "HUFA_percent",
        "SFA_percent",
        "MeanChainLength",
        "VLCFA_percent"
      )
  ) %>%

  group_by(Gene) %>%

  summarise(

    StructuralPhenotypeStrength =
      sqrt(
        mean(
          effect_median^2,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      ),

    ReproducibleFraction =
      mean(
        reproducible,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    gene_replicate_score,
    by = "Gene"
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    desc(
      StructuralPhenotypeStrength
    )
  )


print(
  saturation_priority,
  n = Inf
)
```

## The outputs I would pay most attention to

For your LTP screen, I think the most informative combination will be **five separate phenotypes**, rather than trying to reduce saturation into one number:

* `UnsaturationIndex` — mean double bonds per resolved fatty-acyl chain.
* `PUFA_percent` — fraction of resolved fatty-acyl moles with ≥2 double bonds.
* `HUFA_percent` — fraction with ≥4 double bonds, which should make 20:4/20:5/22:6-type effects more visible.
* `MeanChainLength` and `VLCFA_percent` — likely particularly informative for membrane trafficking phenotypes.
* Individual FA changes such as **16:0, 18:1, 18:2, 20:4, 22:6, 24:0 and 24:1**.

The other part I would retain is the distinction between **absolute fatty-acyl amount** and **fatty-acyl percentage**. If 20:4-PC goes up because total PC doubles, that is a different phenotype from PC remaining constant but being remodelled from 18:1 toward 20:4.

And for your unreliable replicates, I would use the QC workflow exactly as above: **flag → inspect raw replicate points → manually exclude by `SampleKey` or by gene/sample/class**. I would not use an automated outlier-removal algorithm with only ~3 biological replicates, because it is too easy to delete a genuine strong biological phenotype.
